title: purge: see the directories an earlier layout left behind
description: This one probably requires some thinking.
commit_message:
purge: see the directories an earlier layout left behind

purge() only ever lists the current publish_base, so date directories
sitting where the old code wrote them are outside its reach forever.
Meanwhile manifest_files() walks the whole tree and yields anything under
a "current" or "pending" directory, so the orphaned "current" symlink
keeps advertising those images.  The result is a build that is at once
unreapable and still published: a tree holding both layouts lists the
same product twice, one entry pointing at a build from years ago that a
one-day purge just declined to touch.

Neither ADT-1907 nor ADT-1911 shipped a migration, and nothing else reaps
these, so add legacy_publish_bases: the directories this publisher used
to write to, in both shapes (no series component, and Ubuntu at the tree
root), that still exist.  purge() now walks them too, drains them by the
same age rule, and removes each one once its last build is gone -- what
is left by then is dangling symlinks and Apache index files, and it is
the dangling "current" that the manifest walks into.

POLICY CHOICE FOR REVIEW: reporting is the default.  These are
directories the running code has never written and an operator may be
keeping them on purpose, so purge() logs what it would remove and does
nothing until CDIMAGE_PURGE_LEGACY is set.  Run it once with that unset,
read the warnings, and only then turn it on.  It also refuses to act on a
count-only configuration: "keep the newest N" says nothing about how old
is too old, which is not a rule to drain an abandoned tree with.

Within a legacy base "current" and "pending" no longer preserve anything,
since nothing publishes there; a "manual" symlink still does, so
is_pinned now takes the set of pins that count.  ubuntu-core's
channel-based layout was untouched by both changes and has no legacy
location.

+    def make_legacy_base(self, publisher, dates, current=True):
+        """Populate the pre-ADT-1907 publication directory for a publisher."""
+        base = os.path.join(publisher.tree.project_base, publisher.image_type)
+        for name in dates:
+            touch(os.path.join(base, name, "file"))
+        if current:
+            os.symlink(dates[-1], os.path.join(base, "current"))
+        return base
+
+    @mock.patch("time.time", return_value=date_to_time("20130321"))

+        # Both shapes an earlier layout could have left behind, and only

+        publisher = self.make_publisher("ubuntu", "daily")
+        self.assertEqual([], publisher.legacy_publish_bases)
+        no_series = os.path.join(publisher.tree.project_base, "daily")
+        os.makedirs(no_series)
+        # Ubuntu also used to publish at the tree root, not under ubuntu/.

+            publisher.tree.directory, Series.latest().full_name, "daily"
+        )
+        os.makedirs(root_rooted)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [no_series, root_rooted], publisher.legacy_publish_bases
+        )
+
+    @mock.patch("time.time", return_value=date_to_time("20130321"))
+    def test_purge_reports_legacy_layout_but_leaves_it(self, *args):
+        # Reporting is the default: these are directories the running code
+        # has never written, so we don't delete them unasked.
+        publisher = self.make_publisher("ubuntu", "daily")
+        touch(os.path.join(publisher.publish_base, "20130321", "file"))
+        legacy = self.make_legacy_base(publisher, ["20130318", "20130319"])
+        self.write_purge_config(days=1)
+        self.capture_logging()
+        publisher.purge()
+        self.assertCountEqual(
+            ["20130318", "20130319", "current"], os.listdir(legacy)
+        )
+        self.assertIn(
+            "%s holds 2 image set(s) from an earlier layout, older than 1 "
+            "days and not manually pinned.  Set CDIMAGE_PURGE_LEGACY=1 to "
+            "purge them." % legacy,
+            self.captured_log_messages(),
+        )
+
+    @mock.patch("time.time", return_value=date_to_time("20130321"))
+    def test_purge_legacy_layout_when_asked(self, *args):
+        # Draining it removes the directory entirely: its "current" symlink
+        # is what keeps stale images in the site manifest.
+        publisher = self.make_publisher("ubuntu", "daily")
+        touch(os.path.join(publisher.publish_base, "20130321", "file"))
+        legacy = self.make_legacy_base(publisher, ["20130318", "20130319"])
+        self.write_purge_config(days=1)
+        self.config["CDIMAGE_PURGE_LEGACY"] = "1"
+        self.capture_logging()
+        publisher.purge()
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(legacy))
+        self.assertCountEqual(["20130321"], os.listdir(publisher.publish_base))
+
+    @mock.patch("time.time", return_value=date_to_time("20130321"))
+    def test_purge_legacy_layout_keeps_manual_pin(self, *args):
+        # "current" and "pending" there are stale automatic pointers, but a
+        # "manual" symlink is a deliberate decision and still counts.
+        publisher = self.make_publisher("ubuntu", "daily")
+        touch(os.path.join(publisher.publish_base, "20130321", "file"))
+        legacy = self.make_legacy_base(publisher, ["20130318", "20130319"])
+        os.symlink("20130318", os.path.join(legacy, "manual"))
+        self.write_purge_config(days=1)
+        self.config["CDIMAGE_PURGE_LEGACY"] = "1"
+        self.capture_logging()
+        publisher.purge()
+        # The pinned build stays, and the "current" symlink whose target
+        # just went is removed rather than left dangling.
+        self.assertCountEqual(["20130318", "manual"], os.listdir(legacy))
+
+    @mock.patch("time.time", return_value=date_to_time("20130321"))
+    def test_purge_legacy_layout_needs_purge_days(self, *args):
+        # A count-only configuration says how many to keep, not how old is
+        # too old; that isn't a rule to drain an abandoned tree with.
+        publisher = self.make_publisher("ubuntu", "daily")
+        touch(os.path.join(publisher.publish_base, "20130321", "file"))
+        legacy = self.make_legacy_base(publisher, ["20130318", "20130319"])
+        self.write_purge_config(count=1)
+        self.config["CDIMAGE_PURGE_LEGACY"] = "1"
+        self.capture_logging()
+        publisher.purge()
+        self.assertCountEqual(
+            ["20130318", "20130319", "current"], os.listdir(legacy)
+        )
+        self.assertIn(
+            "%s holds images from an earlier layout, but no purge-days is "
+            "configured for ubuntu/daily; not purging them." % legacy,

+        )

+    def legacy_publish_bases(self):
+        """Directories this publisher used to publish to, that still exist.
+
+        Two layout changes moved daily publications without moving what the
+        old code had already written: ADT-1907 nested the devel series under
+        <series>/, and ADT-1911 moved Ubuntu out of the tree root and under
+        <project>/.  Neither shipped a migration, so build directories are
+        still sitting in these paths, outside the reach of purge() and of
+        anything else that works from publish_base.
+
+        The ubuntu-core channel layout was untouched by both, so it has no
+        legacy location.
+        """
+        if (
+            self.config.project
+            in ("ubuntu-core", "ubuntu-core-desktop", "ubuntu-appliance")
+            and self.image_type == "daily-live"
+        ):
+            return []
+        image_type_path = self.image_type.replace("_", "/")
+        roots = [self.tree.project_base]
+        if self.config.project == "ubuntu":
+            # Before ADT-1911, project_base for Ubuntu was the tree root.
+            roots.append(self.tree.directory)
+        bases = []
+        for root in roots:
+            for tail in (
+                # Post-ADT-1907 shape, under the pre-ADT-1911 root.
+                os.path.join(self.config.full_series, image_type_path),
+                # Pre-ADT-1907 shape: no series component at all.
+                image_type_path,
+            ):
+                base = os.path.join(root, tail)
+                if base != self.publish_base and base not in bases:
+                    bases.append(base)
+        return [base for base in bases if os.path.isdir(base)]
